Male bullet. BLUE NET 1 = THE BRAKE CIRCUIT - 0.0 Ohm to B04.2 and 0.1 Ohm to B10.4 on 2026-08-28. Consistent with W_BRK_OUT_F: front brake switch output entering the harness at the headlight junction; running to the B04.2 merge and on to the tail lamp

Longer run (240mm) to a DOUBLE-FEMALE BULLET - one harness wire in the crimp; both slots EMPTY. Larger gauge than the common wire. YELLOW base with black tracer. GROUND NET A - 0.2 Ohm to the B04.1 chassis ring 2026-08-28

Longer run (240mm) to a DOUBLE-FEMALE BULLET - one harness wire in the crimp; both slots EMPTY. WHITE base with blue tracer. SAME NET AS B09 - 0.3 Ohm 2026-08-28; one net seen at both ends. Not in the cable index

Male bullet MATED TO THE HEADLIGHT PIGTAIL. RED base with yellow tracer - NOT Y/R. R/Y is a dimmer beam output in the switch table; with B00.12 (R/BK) this is one of the two headlight filament feeds. mate_class = subharness (headlight pigtail)

TWO green wires crimped into ONE female bullet - a 2-to-1 shared-crimp splice. GREEN NET - 0.3 Ohm to B00.1's green on 2026-08-28. Green is the left-turn circuit (SIG_L); mirrors B00.4 on the grey side

DOUBLE-FEMALE BULLET - one harness wire in the crimp; both slots EMPTY. BROWN base with white tracer. ** PROCEDURE ITEM 0b CLOSED 2026-08-28 **: Br/W rings continuous across B01.2 (RH_4P) B00.11 and B06.5 with the RH 4P DISCONNECTED - so this is one harness net running right-bar 4P to headlight junction to fuse box; not a colour coincidence. ** IMPLIES A HIDDEN INTERNAL JUNCTION **: this terminal holds ONE wire and both its slots are empty; one wire cannot reach three endpoints; so the Br/W runs to B01.2 and B06.5 are joined by a splice or shared crimp INSIDE the harness under the tape. Location unknown - find it in Step 3. Resistance not recorded

wires: Br Br/W Y/R BK (base colour first as read). Its BK is BLACK NET 2 - 0.2 Ohm to B06.2 (starter relay branch) and OPEN to the horn net; consistent with the start button. Colour matches RH_4P 4-of-4 in the cable index. Its Br/W rings continuous to B00.11 and B06.5 (fuse box) with this connector DISCONNECTED - see item 0b closure

HORN - wires Br BK on a pair of individual spade terminals. Its BK is BLACK NET 1 - 0.1 Ohm to B02.1 at the left-bar junction on 2026-08-28; the horn button return. Its Br is on the single brown switched-ignition net. Identified at the bench 2026-08-28 by elimination: the bar switches carry their own pigtails that come down to meet the main harness at B01.2 (the 4P) so nothing bar-mounted hangs off B01 directly; front brake switch is on that pigtail not here. Horn is untranscribed (#9) so its absence from the cable index is expected. BLUE NET 1 - 0.0 Ohm to B00.6 and continuous to B10.4 on 2026-08-28. CONFIRMED as SP_BRAKE

NEUTRAL SWITCH LEAD - identified at the bench 2026-08-28 with the wire in hand; pending ring-out confirmation. Recorded as LG not GN: Kawasaki LG and G both render GN in the models so GN here would lose the distinction

B02 is a zero-length fork at the trunk - confirmed at the bench 2026-08-28: all 3 children split at B02 exactly. Single black wire on an individual SPADE terminal. ** BLACK NET 1 = HORN BUTTON RETURN ** - 0.1 Ohm to B01.3's black (the horn) on 2026-08-28 and OPEN to black net 2. B02 is the left-bar junction and the switch table gives the horn button as BK to ground; so this is the horn's return leg up to the button on the left switch

Single blue wire on a BULLET connector. ** BLUE NET 2 ** - OPEN to the brake circuit (B00.6/B04.2/B10.4) and 0.1 Ohm to B06.5's blue (the fuse box 4P) on 2026-08-28. So this is a FUSED FEED reaching the left-bar junction; with the dimmer sitting on the left switch (R/BK . Bl . R/Y) it is the headlight supply into the dimmer common. First reading of the B02.2-B06.5 pair was 23 Ohm; the terminal face was scraped and the remeasure gave 0.1 Ohm - both recorded per the append-never-overwrite rule

LEFT-HAND SWITCHGEAR 6P connector (candidate). Wires as read: red/black grey orange green red/yellow brown. Model LH carries only 3 of these (orange green grey = W_FLASH_OUT W_SIG_L W_SIG_R); red/black red/yellow brown are the headlight/dimmer circuit which is untranscribed (#9). Confirms the dimmer sits on the LEFT switch. On 2026-08-28 its green rings 0.0 Ohm and its grey 0.5 Ohm to the matching wires at B00.1; its brown is on the single brown switched-ignition net

Single wire off the trunk - no children. Terminates in a DOUBLE-FEMALE BULLET TERMINAL: one harness wire in the crimp; the terminal presents TWO receptacle slots and BOTH ARE EMPTY. The harness contributes a single wire - the two legs it fed are EXTERNAL male bullets unplugged at teardown and not recorded. ** Y/R NET 1 ** - 0.2 Ohm to B01.2 (RH_4P) on 2026-08-28 and OPEN to B06.1 which is a separate Y/R circuit. Consistent with SP_YR: kill-switch output via the right-bar 4P feeding the coils. The first reading of the B03-B01.2 pair drifted 30 Ohm falling to 12 Ohm and was rejected as bad probe contact; the remeasure gave 0.2 Ohm. Both recorded per the append-never-overwrite rule

Runs 200mm as a bundle then forks into several children - each child breaks out at 200 along B04. wire_count DEFERRED TO STEP 3: the bundle is still taped and the count is not visible without unwrapping. Sum the children's counts now as a prediction and check it when the loom comes off - a mismatch means a splice inside these 200mm

RING TERMINAL. Y/BK = YELLOW base with a thin BLACK tracer. Confirmed with certainty at the bench 2026-08-28 as distinct from the BLACK-base wires on B04.3/B04.5. GROUND NET A (yellow base) - rings 0.2 Ohm to B00.7 and B08 and OPEN to every black-base ground 2026-08-28. Gauge in the 14-18 band - definitively NOT 6 AWG; this is therefore NOT W_BAT_GND (modelled 6 AWG BATT->GND_CHASSIS). The battery earth cable appears not to be part of this loom at all. Docs record exactly one ring terminal on the whole harness so this is the small-circuit chassis ground. Yellow base here vs BKYE (black base) on every modelled ground - see the colour-change hypothesis in measurements/README

TWO blue wires crimped into ONE bullet terminal - a 2-to-1 MERGE. Electrically a splice; mechanically a shared crimp. Strong candidate for SP_BRAKE (front + rear brake switch outputs merging to feed the tail lamp; W_BRK_OUT_F W_BRK_OUT_R W_BRAKE are all BU). BLUE NET 1 - 0.0 Ohm to B00.6 and continuous to B10.4 on 2026-08-28. CONFIRMED as SP_BRAKE

Wires as read: BK/Y (BLACK base; thin yellow tracer); yellow (18 AWG); yellow (18 AWG); brown. Connector: 4-PIN RECTANGULAR HOUSING with 4 flat female spade terminals; make/series unidentified (blade width not yet measured - needed for part selection). ** CONFIRMED AS THE REGULATOR/RECTIFIER CONNECTOR (RR) 2026-08-28 ** - both yellow slots ring through to the B05 alternator phase bullets. Br + BK/Y + 2x Y is the classic Kawasaki R/R set (AC phases in; DC out on Br; ground on BK/Y). The model has RR carrying YE YE WH BK. Single-phase alternator so the 4 pins are 2 AC in + DC out + ground with no spare: brown IS the DC output. It rings 0.0 Ohm to the ignition switch brown 2026-08-28 so charging returns to the battery through the ignition switch. W_RR_OUT is therefore wrong on BOTH colour (brown not white) and destination (the brown switched net not SOL) ** NOTE OVERTURNED 2026-08-29 (geometry unchanged, status unchanged). ** The claim above that brown IS the DC output, and that charging returns through the ignition switch, is WRONG. It rested on 'no spare pin'; the R/R half of this 4P is populated on THREE cavities only and the BROWN CAVITY IS EMPTY. The SH221-12's fourth lead leaves as a W/R male bullet to B04.6. Blade width now measured: 5.96/5.97 mm, parallel full length. Cavity map and full detail in connector-inventory.csv.

Female bullet. BK/Y = BLACK base with a thin YELLOW tracer. Confirmed distinct from B04.1 (yellow base) at the bench 2026-08-28

Female bullet. Male bullet; WHITE base with red tracer. ** EVIDENCE OF MELTING / CORROSION **. SAME NET AS B04.6 - 0.1 Ohm 2026-08-28 ** UPDATED 2026-08-29: harness side is a SINGLE MALE BULLET ** - confirmed with the starter and fuse-block cables disconnected. 4-pin RECTANGULAR connector. MATE (recorded 2026-08-28 while still connected): a DIRECT FIXED PIGTAIL off the FUSE BOX. Its taped bundle also gathers the mating wires of B06.3 and B06.4; all of it runs to the fuse box. mate_class = component (fuse box). Which holder it lands on is the remaining question and belongs to the fuse box ring-out (item 0b part C). R/Bl does not appear in the cable index
